small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_SP configs (256) and try BLOCK_OC=64 fixed (not power-of-2 padded beyond OC=64) with num_warps=8, num_stages=3 to amortize the KH*KW=9 outer loop and weight loads.
- Cache weights once outside the kh/kw loops by loading the full [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC, KH, KW] tile (KH=KW=3, IC=16, OC=64 is tiny — ~36KB) into registers/SMEM, eliminating redundant weight reloads across spatial tiles. Alternatively reorder so weight is loaded once per (kh,kw) but x is the inner contiguous load.
- Switch x loads to use stride_xw=1 contiguity by tiling spatial along W only (BLOCK_OW contiguous) rather than flattened OH*OW, so input reads coalesce better across the BLOCK_SP dimension and ih,iw arithmetic simplifies.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM where the K dimension is IC*KH*KW=144 (already small) and reduce min/tanh fused in the epilogue: one program computes a [BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP] output tile with a single K-loop over 144 elements, then does a tl.min over OC and writes one output. This removes the nested static_range over kh,kw and lets tl.dot run on a single large GEMM tile.
- Consider a "no-GEMM" direct conv: since OC=64 fits in registers and KH*KW=9 is tiny, one program per (N, spatial-tile) with BLOCK_SP=128, holding a [64, 128] accumulator, looping IC=16 and unrolling 3x3. The min-reduction is then a single tl.min across the register tile — avoids tl.dot overhead for this small K.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the IC axis is the contiguous innermost dim; gives coalesced loads for the inner IC reduction and matches the natural GEMM-K direction.
